title: City Council District 9
statement: Laurel is moving in the right direction — sentiment up to 0.05 from -0.15, crime index down to 0.65 — but decay momentum remains and retail vitality slipped to 5.7. The patch and clean-up is still in announced, and the C116 legislation-filing deadline was missed. This week I'm answering the Planning Director's directive with the record I have, and I'm putting the work move on the board: completing scope and outreach and getting a Clerk-verified filing so residents can check it themselves. I'm not going to treat a budget line as the finish line.

payload.text: Director Vance — here is the record separated as you asked. The Laurel Neighborhood Patch and Clean-Up (INIT-015) remains in announced status with the six-million-dollar budget unspent; the C116 legislation-filing deadline was missed, and scope, outreach and a Clerk-verified filing are still outstanding. That is the overdue legislation side. The missed-pickup recovery and the four district complaints are tracked separately in the C114–C116 complaint window — Grand Lake incident-table filing (Uptown, C115), the Laurel outreach complaint (C114), the Laurel calls-vs-numbers post (C114), and the Coliseum rider filing (Laurel, C114). I do not have a completed service-status record to hand you; what I have is the announcement and the missed filing. My commitment this cycle is to complete scope and outreach and obtain the Clerk-verified filing, so the next record you see from my office is verifiable, not asserted.
